questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a good social university and had interesting modules

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Leeds have a easy website that guides you through all the things you need to know

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt need anything but we had lecture and a lot of news letters that had the information that was needed if you had any questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was through the university, but it wasnt on campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived on Devonshire hall which was a social old Hall. A 15 min walk from campus trough a nice park. A lot of young students lived there and its conditions was pretty old, but mostly nice. It was really expensive so you can defently find something cheaper closer to campus, but I dont regret staying there

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had to sent a lot of papers a few times because the information on how you needed to sent them was clear

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a system that you just follow and with video guides

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Video guides

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try some diffrent fun modules, its a gamble! The module that you thought would be very boring can end of being the best!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The programme is very diffrent from what I'm used to in Denmark. A lot of reading and very few classes that can be really good or the worst classes ever

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was a appropriate level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything was different. If you really want to learn anything you need to read everything and that is just a lof of selfstudy without the correct amount of classes where you can disscus the topics. The teachers where very passionate and skillful, but not always good at teaching. I took a lot with me, but you need to prioritate studying a lot, to get the same out of it as you might get at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Love, Ethics. Managing classroom behaviour. Children, young people, families and the state. Decolonising development and disability.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I LOOOOVED Decolonising development and disability! So passionate teachers and a courses that I will remember the rest of my life. The excam was also fun because it was a learing journal with a lot of reflections. 

Love, Ethics was also so interesting and fun, but also very challenging if you are not used to Philosophy. Every other week we had a small seminar class where we would sit around 5 people talking about love.

questions.answer: Im not really sure about the cost but it should be around this amount. I lived at a catered accomondation so the food was inclued in the housing. The rest was for weekends and lunch

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! there was clubs and socities for everything!!!!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just try as much as possible in the beginning! Maybe go to the Global cafe and meet other people on exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Leeds have a perfect location to go around the UK. You can easily travel to other big cities or go hiking. I really liked the small town Haworth where the Bronte sisters lived.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, but didnt meet a lot of locals. I meet mostly other people on exchange

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The societies are a good oppotuinty to meet locals. The nordic society was lots of fun and all the nerd ones too

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: driving on the left.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone in north england are so sweet, hospitable and social. I love how they go to the pub everynight and are not afraid to small talk.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore all of the UK while you are there but remember to also just enjoy Leeds because it has so much to offer. Rent a bike the public transport is expensive. Have a go to coffee place, so you can be friends with the barista.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is something for everyone at Leeds and maybe try to go to there ball

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the most amazing people that I will be friends with for life! I have friends all over the world now!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That everyone was younger than I and that the exchange students that came from countries far away wanted to travel a lot so we didnt have normal experience of being a local in a city the same way, if that make sense?

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
